name: Visapur Fort
epithet: पेशवेकालीन दुर्ग — Twin Plateau Fortress of Lohagad
shortDesc: Twin fort companion to Lohagad, celebrated for its monsoon waterfall staircase climbs, massive stone grinders, and sweeping 1,084 m plateau ramparts.
overviewTitle: The Expansive High Plateau Above Lohagad
overviewP1: Built between 1713 and 1720 CE by Balaji Vishwanath, the first Peshwa of the Maratha Empire, Visapur Fort crowns the eastern half of the same volcanic tableland as Lohagad but rises 51 meters higher (1,084 m) with a far broader fortified perimeter.
overviewP2: During the Sahyadri monsoon, the rock-cut eastern staircase turns into a cascading stream, making it one of Maharashtra's most iconic rain treks. Atop the plateau stand Peshwa wada ruins, Hanuman carvings, an iron cannon, and giant stone mortar mills (Chunam Ghani).

architecturalPillars.title: Continuous Outer Curtain Wall
architecturalPillars.desc: Unlike Lohagad's natural cliff reliance, Visapur's entire massive plateau rim is ringed by dressed basalt ramparts.

architecturalPillars.title: Chunam Mortar Mills
architecturalPillars.desc: Massive circular stone grinding troughs turned by oxen to mix lime, jaggery, and bel-fruit mortar during fort construction.

infobox.quote: Because Visapur stood 160 feet higher than Lohagad, British batteries placed here in 1818 forced Lohagad's surrender.

sites.name: Monsoon Waterfall Staircase (धबधबा पायरी मार्ग)
sites.subtitle: Rock-Cut Ravine Ascent Along the Southern Escarpment
sites.desc: Chiseled steps ascending through a basalt gorge that carries clear mountain runoff from July to September.

timeline.title: 1713–1720 — Built by First Peshwa Balaji Vishwanath
timeline.desc: Constructed under Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj's reign to reinforce Lohagad and prevent enemies from occupying the higher eastern plateau.

routes.title: Patan Village / Gaymukh Trail
routes.desc: Scenic forest and rock-step climb from Patan village or the Gaymukh saddle between Lohagad and Visapur.
